summary: London Biggin Hill Airport is a private general aviation facility located on the crest of the North Downs in southeast London, within the Borough of Bromley. Originally established as an airfield during the First World War, it became one of the most celebrated Royal Air Force fighter stations of the Battle of Britain in 1940. Today it serves primarily business aviation, private jets, and flight training, ranking among the busiest dedicated business airports in the UK.
faqs:
Q: Are there commercial passenger flights from Biggin Hill?
A: No, the airport does not serve scheduled commercial flights. It is focused on private, charter, and business aviation only.

Q: How far is Biggin Hill from central London?
A: The airport is approximately 15 miles (24 km) southeast of central London, depending on your route and traffic conditions.

Q: Does the airport have a control tower?
A: Yes, Biggin Hill has an operating air traffic control tower, which is unusual for a general aviation airport and supports its role in handling business jet traffic.

Q: What was the airport's role in World War II?
A: It was an RAF fighter station heavily involved in the Battle of Britain in 1940 and was bombed by the Luftwaffe on multiple occasions.
transport_tips: The airport is best reached by car via the A21 and A233, with ample on-site parking available for both short and long stays. Taxi and pre-booked private transfer services are the most reliable options from central London, typically taking 45 to 75 minutes depending on traffic. There is no direct rail or London Underground service, so most visitors use a combination of train to Bromley South followed by a short taxi ride.
local_tip: If you have time before a flight, visit the Biggin Hill Heritage Hangar nearby, which preserves aircraft and memorabilia from the airport's Battle of Britain history—a hidden gem most travelers flying through never see.
